request.system: You check whether a piece of evidence can bear on a claim at all. You are given a claim quoted from a vendor's own materials, a quote from an independent source, and the relation someone proposed between them. Do not judge whether the proposed relation is the right one. Judge only whether the evidence could bear on the claim. First state what property the claim asserts and about what scope: which products, people, period or population it covers. Then state what the evidence measures or reports, and about what scope. same_property is true only when both are about the same property: the same capability, metric, feature or fact. Sharing a subject or a topic is not enough. comparable_scope is true when a conclusion about the claim can follow from the evidence at the evidence's scope. Scope is not size. A single case can show that something exists or can happen, so it can bear on a claim that something exists or is possible. A single case cannot establish or refute a rate, an average, a trend or a claim about a whole population. Evidence about part of a population bears on a claim about the whole only when the claim is about every member.

messages.content:
Claim, quoted from the vendor's own materials:
"The complaint alleges that the defendants made material misrepresentations and omissions about the Company’s Autopilot and FSD Capability technologies"

Evidence, quoted from an independent source:
"In August 2022, records surfaced showing that the California DMV had formally accused Tesla of false advertising Autopilot and FSD in July.[51]"

Proposed relation: the evidence corroborates the claim.

parsed_output.claim_property: The content of a specific legal complaint's allegations \u2014 namely that the named defendants made material misrepresentations and omissions regarding Tesla's Autopilot and FSD Capability technologies
parsed_output.claim_scope: One particular filed lawsuit (a securities/shareholder complaint) against the Company and certain individual defendants, limited to what that pleading asserts
parsed_output.evidence_property: The existence of a separate regulatory action: the California DMV's formal accusation that Tesla engaged in false advertising of Autopilot and FSD
parsed_output.evidence_scope: A single state agency proceeding, filed July 2022 and reported in August 2022, concerning Tesla's marketing of Autopilot/FSD in California
